newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finance minister welcomes Senate's tax vote.
newsitem.headline: Polish finance minister welcomes Senate's tax vote.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko welcomed on Thursday the Senate's vote to reject a proposal for a deep cut in next year's personal income tax for the most needy, which he has said would hit public finances.
"The Senate's decision is wise and compatible with solutions proposed by the government," Kolodko told reporters after the vote, which coincided with a launch of a dabate on next year's budget draft.
The upper house voted 44 to 33 with nine abstentions to lower 1997 tax levels to 20, 32 and 44 percent from the current 21, 33 and 45 percent.

It thus rejected the lower house' proposal to introduce a four level scale of 17, 20, 33 and 45 percent, which the finance ministry earlier said would require to either radically slash spending or boost the budget deficit beyond limits.
Under income patterns in Poland changes in the lowest bracket of personal taxes has the biggest impact on budget revenues.
According to finance ministry figures provided earlier this month, the senate's tax levels would allow to maintain the 1997 budget deficit at about 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
Government's earlier proposal to lower the tax levels to 20, 32 and 43 percent, rejected by the lower house, would have envisaged a similar gap.
The lower house is expected to hold a final vote on the 1997 taxes next week and may still reject the Senate's decision.
